  • raise ExporterUnavailable / ImporterUnavailable when a dependency is missing, e.g. native binaries or libraries
    • 

  • raise NotImplementedError for features that are not implemented yet
    • 

  • do not modify the scene or the options passed in
    • 







11.2.4 PEX25D Exporters


An exporter writes the input files of a solver from a resolved PEX25DScene (see Section 11.1.2), it does not run the solver:


class PEX25DSceneExporter(Protocol):
    @classmethod
    def supported_capabilities(cls) -> FrozenSet[SceneCapability]:
        return frozenset()

    def export(self,
               scene: PEX25DScene,
               *,
               output_dir_path: str,
               prefix: str = '',
               options: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> List[str]:
        ...


    

  • scene: the resolved scene (pex25d export resolves a PEX25DFile first)
    • 

  • output_dir_path: the directory for the files, the exporter creates it if necessary
    • 

  • prefix: prefix for the file names, an empty prefix means the exporter’s own default
    • 

  • options: exporter specific options, e.g. from --option
    • 

  • returns the paths of the files written, the main input file first
    • 



A minimal exporter, which writes the net of each conductor into a text file:


import os
from typing import Any, List, Mapping, Optional

from klayout_pex.plugin_api.v1 import ExportError, PEX25DSceneExporter


class NetsExporter(PEX25DSceneExporter):
    def export(self, scene, *, output_dir_path: str, prefix: str = '',
               options: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> List[str]:
        if options:
            raise ExportError(f"unknown options: {', '.join(options)}")
        os.makedirs(output_dir_path, exist_ok=True)
        path = os.path.join(output_dir_path, f"{prefix}nets.txt")
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            for conductor in scene.conductors:
                file.write(f"{conductor.name} {conductor.net}\n")
        return [path]


def create_exporter() -> NetsExporter:
    return NetsExporter()




11.2.4.1 Preserve Scene Capabilities


The host checks required scene capabilities before invoking an exporter.


The supported_capabilities() class method returns a FrozenSet[SceneCapability]: an immutable set of typed enum members. Support can be queried on the class without constructing an exporter or loading its optional geometry dependencies. Derived exporters can extend super().supported_capabilities().


The default method returns an empty set. Structural implementations without the method also support only scenes requiring no additional capabilities. They cannot silently consume required geometry, electrical-identity or accounting semantics.


A physical exporter must preserve both the reference geometry and the electrical ownership described in Section 11.1.5.4. The geometry and ownership contracts are:


    

  • GROUND_CUTOUTS means the exporter subtracts the complete opening geometry from the reference slab and preserves the corresponding coating geometry
    • 

  • ELECTRICAL_IDENTITY means it respects the reference net and keeps independent floating bodies distinct from named nets
    • 



Declaring a capability is a promise that the exporter implements it. A scene requiring an undeclared capability is rejected before export. Solver labels may need disambiguation; preserve the returned body-name mapping alongside the solver artifacts.


Use the shared helpers for the same geometry and ownership rules as the built-in exporters. Given a resolved scene and a finite field_region in the scene’s integer coordinate grid:


from klayout_pex.plugin_api.v1 import (
    ground_body,
    retained_ground_region,
    solver_body_names,
)

labels = solver_body_names(scene)
reference_name = labels[ground_body(scene)]
reference_region = retained_ground_region(
    scene.ground_plane, field_region
)


ground_body and conductor_body return an ElectricalBody. Its BodyKind distinguishes a named net (NET) from an independent floating body (FLOATING_BODY). The identity does not depend on label spelling. retained_ground_region subtracts the union of openings while preserving their islands. write_solver_body_map writes the label mapping when disambiguation is needed.


The geometry helpers use KLayout regions when called. Importing the public helper names does not load that optional geometry backend, so plugin discovery can remain independent of it.






11.2.4.2 Capacitance Accounting







An exporter whose export() implements the complete accounting contract overrides the class method:


from typing import FrozenSet
from klayout_pex.plugin_api.v1 import (
    PEX25DSceneExporter, SceneCapability,
)


class AccountingExporter(PEX25DSceneExporter):
    @classmethod
    def supported_capabilities(cls) -> FrozenSet[SceneCapability]:
        return frozenset({
            SceneCapability.CAPACITANCE_ACCOUNTING,
        })


An exporter declares every contract it implements. All capabilities required by a scene must be supported; declaring an unrelated capability cannot substitute for a missing one. The built-in FasterCap and FastCap2 exporters declare all three. The STL exporter declares the two geometry and electrical-identity contracts, so it rejects accounting scenes.


Declaring the capability alone does not implement support. The exporter must distinguish physical electrical bodies from charge-accounting parts, preserve accounting_part_id and accounting_regions, and keep the physical reference body distinct from routing on the same net. Parts of a connected NET retain one potential; splitting their accounting identity must not introduce another independent physical terminal.


The built-in FasterCap/FastCap2 path records the accounting map alongside solver input and uses it when consuming the matrix. A plugin that cannot carry that meaning through its solver and result consumer must leave that capability undeclared. The host then rejects the scene before the plugin writes output. Unknown protobuf required-capability values are rejected independently of the plugin’s declaration.


See Section 11.1.5.7 for the text records, exact-grid rules and runnable example. These policies do not infer intrinsic compact-device capacitance ownership.






11.2.4.3 Example: FEM Solvers Elmer and Palace


As examples for external exporters, we provide plugins for two open source FEM field solvers, both used for capacitance extraction (electrostatics):


    

  • klayout-pex-plugin-elmer: exporter elmer for Elmer FEM (StatElecSolver)
    • 

  • klayout-pex-plugin-palace: exporter palace for Palace (Electrostatic problem)
    • 

  • both use the volume mesh of klayout-pex-plugin-gmsh, which is also available as exporter gmsh
    • 








The mesh is built in these steps:


    

  • 2.5D prisms: the domain is sliced at every z where a solid starts or ends

      

    • within each slab, conductors and the ground plane come first, then the dielectrics by wrap depth (see Section 11.1.5.5), and the background fills the rest
      • 

    • so the prisms fill the domain exactly once
      • 

    • 

  • the prisms are extruded and fragmented using OpenCASCADE, so touching solids share their faces
    • 

  • the conductors are removed, only their surfaces remain, as one physical group per net
    • 

  • the elements are refined at the conductor edges, where the field concentrates

      

    • by default, down to the thickness of the thinnest conductor layer
      • 

    • 



Elmer FEM:


pip3 install --upgrade klayout-pex-plugin-elmer

pex25d export cell.pex25d --to elmer --out-dir elmer
cd elmer
ElmerGrid 14 2 mesh.msh -autoclean   # gmsh mesh -> Elmer mesh
ElmerSolver case.sif                 # writes cmatrix.dat


Palace:


pip3 install --upgrade klayout-pex-plugin-palace

pex25d export cell.pex25d --to palace --out-dir palace
cd palace
palace -np 4 config.json             # writes postpro/terminal-Cm.csv


Both solvers write the capacitance matrix in mutual form:


    

  • off-diagonal cells contain the coupling capacitance between two terminals
    • 

  • diagonal cells contain the capacitance to ground (zero, unless the outer boundary is grounded)
    • 

  • row/column \(i\) belongs to the terminal group with tag \(i\) in mesh.json (nets, floating conductors, ground plane)
    • 



The options of the plugins (mesh sizes, element order, outer boundary condition, …) are listed in the README files of the repositories.












NoteIIC-OSIC-TOOLS







The IIC-OSIC-TOOLS Docker image (see Section 1.5) contains Palace, Elmer FEM is not included yet. When running as root, call palace -serial config.json, as mpirun refuses to run as root.






For the test design overlap_plates_100um_x_100um_m1_m2 (ihp-sg13g2, two plates of 100 µm × 100 µm in Metal1 and Metal2, overlapping by 50 µm × 50 µm), the coupling capacitance between the plates is:






Solver
Mesh
\(C_{LOWER,UPPER}\)






Elmer FEM
default (94k tetrahedra)
181.3 fF




Palace, order 1
same mesh
181.3 fF




Palace, order 2
same mesh

Elmer FEM

A parallel plate estimate of the overlap alone gives 168 fF, the difference being the fringe capacitance.
